teams.heading: Fiji beaten 54-17 in Lyon as France reclaim Northern Hemisphere lead
teams.body: France ran in the points at Lyon on Saturday, and the 54-17 scoreline makes it Fiji's fourth defeat from four logged games. Fiji's squad included 11 players who play in France, a familiarity that did not stop the Bleus. The rout was also marred for France by an injury to Romain Ntamack. Fiji's next opponent, Ireland, beat Argentina by 30 points on Friday night.

lead.why: The result is Fiji's own news, and the match has just been played, so it takes precedence over the Ireland-focused RTÉ piece already covered and the France-side items.

teams.heading: Bill Sweeney backs Steve Borthwick to lead England at 2027 World Cup
teams.body: The RFU's chief executive, Bill Sweeney, has given Steve Borthwick unequivocal backing to lead England at the 2027 World Cup before Sunday's Nations Championship clash with Australia at Twickenham. Sweeney said: "We're committed to Steve. We believe in what he's doing." The RFU extended Borthwick's contract until after the 2028 Six Nations two months ago, although England have lost five of their last seven Tests. Sweeney also accepted a difficult Six Nations, but wants to see continued progress.

lead.why: Formal RFU backing for Borthwick is new union business ahead of Sunday's match, and it is an England story rather than a rival's or a profile.

teams.heading: Dupont and Ntamack start together for first time in 609 days
teams.body: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack started together for France for the first time in 609 days on Saturday, one year and eight months after their last joint start. The reunion came against Fiji, whose 11 players who play in France brought familiarity and physicality to Lyon. France won 54-17, and the Stade de France hosts South Africa later this month.

teams.heading: Craig Casey picked ahead of Jamison Gibson-Park for Argentina Test start
teams.body: Craig Casey was handed the start over Jamison Gibson-Park in midweek and, in RTÉ's player ratings, earned an 8.5 for his display in Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina. Partnered with Sam Prendergast, who scored a solo try and kicked all six conversions, the pair controlled a Test game for the first time together, according to former Ireland scrum-half Conor Murray on the Ireland Rugby Social podcast. Murray added that Prendergast will now have a target on his back.

lead.why: The RTÉ ratings report the midweek half-back change, a new selection angle that the already-reported match and Farrell stories do not cover.

teams.heading: Azzurri concede nine tries in 66-7 defeat to Springboks in Turin
teams.body: Injury-hit Italy were overrun at the Allianz Stadium, where South Africa ran in nine tries, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu contributing a solo try and 21 points, and led 45-0 at half-time. Italy were missing a 16-strong list of unavailable players, including captain Michele Lamaro and centres Tommaso Menoncello and Juan Ignacio Brex, and this was their fourth straight defeat. South Africa, who sit top of the Southern Hemisphere standings on 20 points, next face France in Paris.

teams.heading: Ewan Ashman's first-half hat-trick cannot prevent Scotland's second-half collapse against All Blacks
teams.body: Ewan Ashman's three first-half tries left Scotland only three points down at the break in a 43-21 defeat, but the second half belonged to New Zealand. Josh Moorby, Beauden Barrett and Asafo Aumua scored after the interval while Scotland failed to register a point. Gregor Townsend said the performance fell short of what supporters could be proud of: "And it wasn't there today."

teams.heading: Steve Tandy admits Wales lacked ruthlessness in Japan win despite bonus point
teams.body: Tandy said he could not run away from a below-par performance in which Wales looked flat at times and let Japan stay in the contest, and he put some of the clunkiness down to rust, given it was the first Test since July. Wales now face New Zealand next weekend, and Tandy said his side cannot afford cheap opportunities against the All Blacks. Wales have two wins from four in the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Pumas captain Julián Montoya off with head injury assessment in Dublin defeat
teams.body: Captain Julián Montoya went off for a head injury assessment 28 minutes into Friday's 42-12 defeat in Dublin and never returned to the field. Leonel Oviedo also went off for a head injury assessment on 36 minutes, returning four minutes later. The coverage reports no outcome for either assessment, and nothing on whether Montoya is available for next weekend's test against Italy.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight earns 50th cap as Wallabies name Jeremy Williams at blindside
teams.body: Australia's back row is reshaped for the Test against England at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, with Harry Wilson again captaining from number eight. Jeremy Williams is named at blindside flanker, alongside Fraser McReight, who will earn his 50th cap for Australia. Len Ikitau returns in midfield after missing the last Test under HIA protocols, partnering Isaac Henry, who will play his first Test in the United Kingdom. Taniela Tupou is back among the replacements.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones says Japan missed chances as Wales held on 28-21
teams.body: Japan coach Eddie Jones said the 28-21 defeat in Cardiff was one that got away: "That could have been a historic win for us." Japan levelled the score twice, through Ben Gunter and Warner Dearns, and Shinya Komura's try four minutes from time left Wales holding on by a single score. Jones said his young side stuck at it but did not take points from its time in Wales's 22, which he said is the way the game now works.

lead.why: The most widely reported English-language match account, and the Japan coach's reaction gives it a Japan angle.

teams.heading: All Blacks beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield despite Ewan Ashman's first-half hat-trick
teams.body: Scotland could not score in the second half, and New Zealand ran in seven tries to three at Murrayfield on Saturday. Hooker Ewan Ashman scored a first-half hat-trick, but the All Blacks led 24-21 at the break and their second-half surge settled it, with Josh Moorby, Beauden Barrett and Asafo Aumua scoring after the interval. Wallace Sititi and Peter Lakai both visited the sin bin in the first half. Scotland coach Gregor Townsend said: "And it wasn't there today. So that's frustrating."

lead.why: It is the freshest New Zealand match report in the pack, carried by two outlets, and it covers the result itself rather than the Barrett milestone already run today.

teams.heading: Feinberg-Mngomezulu stars as Boks run in nine tries against Italy in Turin
teams.body: The world champions resumed their Nations Championship campaign in ruthless fashion at Allianz Stadium, where Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu's dazzling solo try set the tone. Italy were missing 16 players through injury, including captain Michele Lamaro, and the Boks led 45-0 at half-time. Marx scored a brace in a nine-try haul that also featured Siya Kolisi and Damian Willemse, and the 66-7 win was a fourth straight bonus-point victory. Next up is France in Paris.
